osaka_sushi_yoshi_minamisenba.notes: [Sushi · Minami-Senba, a six-seat counter known for foie gras and mozzarella nigiri] A calm, wood-toned counter of six seats in a quiet Minami-Senba alley that calls its sushi 'gourmet nigiri': Edomae classics such as lean tuna, kombu-cured anago and a kanpyo roll sit beside foie gras seared on the surface, mozzarella, and water eggplant with sea urchin. The tamago is filled with foie gras, squid and shrimp. Lunch is 10 pieces for ¥5,000 or a ¥12,500 omakase, served quickly by one person; dinner is a course. The pieces are small, and one April 2026 diner found the sweet soy glaze too strong; a long-time fan returns for the foie gras and mozzarella nigiri. A July 2022 diner who had eaten at Sushi Yoshi in Tsuruhashi some 20 years earlier found much the same menu here. Book by phone, from a Japanese mobile number if possible.

chef_bio.philosophy: Creative toppings alongside Edomae-style classics (September 2026 review).

osaka_bistro_umami_shinmachi.notes: [Mediterranean bistro · Shinmachi near Yotsubashi, Middle Eastern meze from a one-person kitchen] A small Santorini-themed bistro on the south side of a Shinmachi apartment block, run by one owner-chef whom reviewers credit with cooking in Dubai and London. Start with the appetizer platter — hummus, orange-marinated beets, tapenade, a carpaccio, sometimes a smoky roasted-eggplant dip or an Aleppo-style red pepper and walnut paste — then the seafood bouillabaisse, saving the broth for the risotto that reviewers insist on. Lamb brochettes over spicy couscous are the official No. 1; the red-wine-braised beef cheek is said to take three days. Since spring 2026 lunch is a pita sandwich set with lentil soup, harissa and tzatziki from about ¥1,000. The wine list leans unusual. Diners call the owner cheerful and willing to talk food at the counter; the room was featured in an・an and Meets, per an October 2025 review. One cook means relaxed pacing, and the counter passage is narrow.

osaka_chinese_yin_yang_hakuromachi.notes: [Chinese · Hakuromachi, a white, stylish room up the back stairs behind the W Osaka] Easy to miss: climb the stairs at the back of an older, well-renovated building and the second floor opens into a bright, modern room with a counter and tables. A January 2025 reviewer called it the second shop of Tokuchaina, and a September 2026 diner who usually goes to Tokuchaina came here for the first time. The cooking is Cantonese-leaning and gently seasoned, with market fish and seasonal vegetables: start with the assorted appetizer platter, then the mapo tofu sharpened with fermented black beans, a fresh-fish carpaccio, stir-fried squid with black beans, shrimp chili or the tom yum fried rice, and finish with a green-onion and char siu noodle soup. Natural wines and Shaoxing run alongside. Weekday lunch is a few sets (mapo tofu, yurinchi, shrimp chili and a weekly special); an April 2026 diner had the special soy-sauce noodles with four small sides for ¥1,200. Dishes come out at a leisurely pace, so order most of it at once.

"The Char Siu Wrapped in Crepe was inspired by Peking Duck. The rich sauce was delicious, and the chewy crepe combined with chunky char siu made for a hearty dish." — October 2026.

osaka_yakiniku_nikutoieba_matsuda_hakuro.notes: [Yakiniku · Hakuromachi, the Osaka counter of a Nara wagyu shop] The Osaka sister of Niku to Ieba Matsuda in Nara, behind a hidden-feeling entrance: a tea-room-like room with a tokonoma-style backdrop, bamboo and a pine-tree neon sign, and a long full-flat counter where the cooking happens in front of you. Yamato beef from Nara is the point. The signature is the thick-cut Chateaubriand tongue, sliced and grilled at the counter; diners also order the Chateaubriand, outside skirt, the truffle yukke and the beef sashimi, and finish with garlic fried rice studded with Chateaubriand. The kitchen also cooks pasta, beef stew, tacos and a katsu sandwich, and a sommelier pours from over 100 wines. Omakase courses run ¥6,000 or ¥11,000. Several October 2026 diners found the service slow on busy nights; one table had a two-hour limit.

chef_bio.philosophy: Yamato beef grilled cut by cut with matching seasonings, alongside genre-crossing dishes from experienced chefs and sommelier-chosen wines (Tabelog, shop-provided).
chef_bio.specialty: Chateaubriand tongue; wagyu truffle yukke; Chateaubriand.

osaka_chinese_azuki_minamisenba.notes: [Chinese · Minamisenba, a small Chinese bar-diner run by a warm couple] Chinese restaurant, bar and diner in one, as one diner puts it: fourteen seats at two-person tables near Nagahoribashi, opened in January 2025. A March 2026 regular credits a husband-and-wife team with the warm, attentive service; another diner was greeted by the friendly woman serving with thanks for an earlier group visit, and says Google suggests 'Azuki Oneesan' when you search the shop. Repeat diners come back for the sweet Shanghai yakisoba, piping-hot xiaolongbao with black vinegar, crisp gyoza, black-vinegar sweet and sour pork and a surprisingly good potato salad with apple; the yurinchi reportedly draws a lunch queue. Lunch is three fixed sets plus a daily special (seafood champon ¥1,200 in February 2026, a mapo curry in April). Courses with all-you-can-drink suit groups, and the whole room can be booked for 20.

osaka_tempura_tenjin_hakuromachi.notes: [Tempura · Hakuromachi, Hakata-style everyday tempura between Honmachi and Shinsaibashi] The name joins Tenjin, the Fukuoka district known for its crowd of casual tempura shops, with 'the god of tempura' (official site). Tempura is fried in 100% rice oil and brought to you a few pieces at a time, so it arrives piping hot: lunch is a set with rice that is cooked continuously in small cookers and refilled free (white or barley), miso soup and homemade daikon pickles on the table. The favourite is the Tamago set, whose soft-boiled egg tempura goes over the rice; others go for 'angel shrimp' (from New Caledonia, one regular heard), kisu, sardines, cheese-stuffed chikuwa or a dorayaki tempura with butter. In the evening, ¥1,000 buys a beer with shrimp, eggplant and chicken tempura. The shop is the only restaurant of Patria Co., whose site names the manager as Takimoto Youhei, from Hokkaido; an August 2026 regular noticed new staff and a new potato salad.

chef_bio.background: Named as manager of the shop on the site of Patria Co., which runs it as its only restaurant from the same address; the site describes a manager who is earnest and passionate rather than high-energy, answers customers' requests in the tempura, and trains the frying staff in a spirit of "no waste, precise". The site is undated, and an August 2026 regular noticed the staff had changed recently. Patria's representative director, 冨安 美絵子 (Tomiyasu Mieko), is from Fukuoka, studied at Saga University aiming to teach art, went into martial arts as a student and after graduating, and founded the company after retiring (operator's site).
chef_bio.philosophy: Freshly fried tempura served straight from the fryer in front of the diner, to make tempura casual and familiar (official site).

osaka_sundubu_shokudo_toshi_shinmachi.notes: [Korean · Shinmachi, sundubu from 11 am to 11:30 pm] A clean, modern 17-seat room on Naniwa-suji, two minutes from Nishi-Ohashi Station, that opened in September 2025 as the second shop of a sundubu restaurant whose first is in Yuzato. The tofu is made in the shop every morning and the broth is wagyu bone and tail with a homemade tategi chili paste; diners call it rich and deep, with clams and a hint of sweetness under the heat. Pick one of eight sundubu (the horumon version is the favourite), a spice level from 0 up, and toppings. At lunch it comes with rice, a raw egg, Korean seaweed and kimchi and namul for about ¥1,000, and the room fills with office workers. Evenings turn into a Korean izakaya: soy- and spice-marinated shrimp that drew a 'What is this? So delicious!' from one table, wagyu yukhoe, chijimi, bulgogi, and makgeolli. The name is read Toshi, not Shun, as one diner learned. It stays open between lunch and dinner, a plus for one regular.

osaka_kacchan_ramen_kitakyuhojimachi.notes: [Ramen · Sakaisuji-Hommachi, chuka soba and free fried rice until 12:30 am] A lively 24-seat shop two minutes from Sakaisuji-Hommachi Station that opened in August 2026 with one hook: every bowl comes with a free mini fried rice, and ¥380 more makes it all-you-can-eat. The operator, an Osaka company that also runs CoCo Ichibanya and Ramen Daisensou franchises, set out to make the town chuka soba of a Showa childhood: house-made noodles and a clear, light broth in shoyu, shio or miso. Diners describe chicken-bone stock with chicken oil, a hint of shellfish and a slightly sweet soy, with thin straight noodles; one called it Tokyo-style with an Osaka twist. The fried rice has drawn YouTubers: refills come out in about two minutes, and diners report going back four or five times, but one late-night diner found it bland and the garlic ramen not hot. After 4 pm a list of Showa diner sides appears, from horse-mackerel fry to red sausages. Cash only at the ticket machine; open daily until 12:30 am.

osaka_stand_sonoda_tanimachi.notes: [Izakaya · Tanimachi 6-chome, the original Sonoda: chashu egg and drinks from 11 am] A lively Showa-retro diner at the end of the Karahori shopping street that opened in 2016, made Tabelog's Izakaya 100 in 2021 and has since spawned branches in Tokyo and Fukuoka. By day office workers pack in for ¥1,000 set meals with free rice refills; at any hour others settle in with a Kohaku Ebisu or a Baisu sour. The dish everyone orders is the chashu egg, tender chashu under a fried egg; then the menchi katsu under aurora sauce, meat tofu, nam-pla-pickled celery and chicken nanban. Many finish with the Chinese soba, a seafood-based shoyu with flat noodles, chashu and clams, which one diner called a bowl you wouldn't expect from a tavern. One diner thinks the site was once a butcher's. Cash only, no bookings, and smoking is allowed after 2 pm. A returning diner found the service slipping on a quiet September 2026 afternoon.

chef_bio.background: Public diner and izakaya that opened on 11 May 2016 (Tabelog); Tabelog Izakaya 100 in 2021 (Tabelog). The main shop of the Sonoda brand, which has expanded to Tokyo and Fukuoka (Time Out Osaka, December 2024). A diner understands it to be a sister shop of Taifuu Hanten nearby, which also serves the chashu egg (September 2026 review).

osaka_sakichan_ramen_minamihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · Minamihonmachi, a yakiniku shop's lunchtime beef-tendon chuka soba] By night a yakiniku and horumon restaurant in the Minamihonmachi office district; at lunch, since September 2024, a ramen counter that puts the yakiniku kitchen's A5 wagyu beef tendon on chuka soba. There are three bowls: the dark, soy-based BLACK, the beef-bone WHITE and the chili-red RED. One diner expected beef and found seafood first: the BLACK is a sweet, seafood-scented shoyu that looks heavier than it tastes, with slow-simmered tendon, chopped onion and green onion, and an egg yolk to stir in. The RED is sweet and spicy with plenty of Korean chili. Noodles are medium and chewy. The plain BLACK was ¥780 in 2025; the Mashi Mashi with extra tendon and green onion ¥1,100, and a ¥350 bowl of tendon bokkake rice finishes the job. The newest review is from September 2025, so check the shop's Instagram first.

chef_bio.background: Lunch-only ramen that opened on 9 September 2024 (Tabelog) inside the yakiniku and horumon restaurant 和ちゃん, which serves yakiniku at night (Instagram @yakiniku.kazuchan; 2025 reviews). A diner credits the bowls to the yakiniku chef (May 2025 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Ramen built on the same wagyu the yakiniku uses; the sign promises the ultimate ramen made with Japanese wagyu beef tendon (April 2025 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Wagyu beef-tendon chuka soba, BLACK, WHITE and RED.

osaka_patisserie_rainette_shinmachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; nearly everything is wheat-flour baking (roll cakes, tarts, pies, cookies, focaccia), though the Tabelog menu lists one cookie, "Coco", as just coconut, egg white and sugar. Ask about shared flour.

Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR in the shop (Tabelog; May 2025 review); the online store takes cards. 13 seats; designated smoking area (Tabelog). Takeout cakes and baked goods. Reservations accepted (Tabelog). One person bakes, serves the café and cooks lunch, and fruit roll cakes and cream puffs are finished to order, so expect a wait (2024–2026 reviews). osaka_patisserie_rainette_shinmachi.notes: [Cake shop and café · Shinmachi, a one-person patisserie since 2007] A small cake shop between Nishi-Ohashi and Yotsubashi that has outlasted the area's fast-changing cafés since 2007, with a motto of sweets that are gentle on body and mind and an online store branded "additive-free sweets". The owner bakes, runs the café and cooks lunch alone, so things take a while: the fruit roll cake is rolled to order and the cream puffs and pies are filled after you ask. Diners single out the apple pie (one was told to try it both warmed and as it is), a moist roll with fresh chocolate cream, a mousse-like lemon pudding and a sweet caramel cheesecake. Light lunches change: a piping-hot bacon-and-mushroom gratin set (¥950, May 2026), and earlier a buckwheat-flour pizza. Prices are low; bring cash.

osaka_kushikatsu_iseda_shinmachi.notes: [Kushikatsu and horumon · Shinmachi, a smoky Showa-style counter by the Orix Theater] A lively kushikatsu izakaya that moved from Kitahorie to a ground-floor spot near the Orix Theater, billing itself as a trip back to the good old Showa era. The batter is light and crisp; diners also go for the grilled offal skewers, a grilled liver with sesame oil and salt, a sweet-spicy Chiri-tori hot pot of beef horumon and vegetables in a square iron pan, and the specialty dote-yaki. Finish with ramen in the pot, cold kimchi noodles, or a cheese risotto. The sauce once came in a shared no-double-dipping pot (2025); by April 2026 it was poured over the plate. A May 2025 group found the owner very pleasant, and later diners felt it was a regulars' place that still made a newcomer feel warmly welcome. Every seat allows smoking, and a 2025 diner found the ventilation weak.

osaka_kurumi_seikaten_shinmachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the shop is built around madeleines, financiers, shell cakes and sablés, which are normally wheat-flour baking. Soft serve is the only other item; ask about its toppings and the shared kitchen.
osaka_kurumi_seikaten_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fermented butter, almonds and honey in the baking, milk soft serve and egg pudding.
osaka_kurumi_seikaten_shinmachi.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–19:00, open all year (Tabelog; shop site). The 3 counter seats inside are by reservation only, and reservations are hard to get; a bench outside when the weather is fine (Tabelog; September–October 2026 reviews). Cards, PayPay, Alipay, WeChat Pay; no e-money (Tabelog). Non-smoking; BYO drinks allowed (Tabelog). A long line wrapped around the street on one September 2026 visit. A freshly baked madeleine or financier is given free with a purchase (September–October 2026 reviews). Opened 18 July 2025 (Tabelog).
osaka_kurumi_seikaten_shinmachi.notes: [Baked sweets · Shinmachi, a madeleine shop with three hard-to-book seats] A tiny shop near the Orix Theater where the smell of fermented butter fills the room and the oven sits in full view. Almost everything is to take away — boxes of madeleines in a dozen flavours (fermented butter, French or Takachiho butter, carrot, chocolate, walnut, Gorgonzola) and the shop's shell cakes — and every purchase comes with one still warm from the oven. The three seats inside are reserved for a light, milky soft serve with a seasonal sauce, or a firm pudding on top of it. Two diners link it with Chihiro Kashiten a few streets away: a September 2026 diner calls it a sister shop, and an October 2026 diner says the logo looks familiar and the shop is run by the son of a former influencer who had sold shares in that shop. A line may wrap the block.

osaka_hawaiian_shokudo_hale_hakuromachi.notes: [Hawaiian · Hakuromachi, build-your-own poke bowls] A bright, wood-toned Hawaiian café between Sakaisuji-Hommachi and Nagahoribashi that has served custom poke bowls since 2019 and bills itself as the first in Osaka to do so. You tick an order sheet: a base of multigrain rice, salad or half and half, two mains such as tuna, salmon or tender roast beef, four sides like avocado, tobiko, edamame and egg yolk, then a sauce; extras push the bill up (one diner reached ¥1,350 in April 2025 and remembers when it was under ¥1,000). Beyond poke there is loco moco, garlic shrimp tender enough to eat shells and all, crisp mochiko chicken and a fruit-heavy açaí bowl, plus a terrace where dogs are welcome. Seating is limited, so weekday lunch can fill up; no reservations.

chef_bio.background: Hawaiian diner that opened on 2 September 2019 (Tabelog), billed by the shop as Osaka's first custom poke bowl specialist (Tabelog, shop-provided). Run by Hawaiisukiyane Co. (ハワイ好きやね株式会社, founded January 2025), which also runs two 3POKE OSAKA shops, SUNNY ISLAND SURF and Hawaiian 8 Market; the company site calls HALE "ここが、はじまりのポキ。" (company site, read October 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Choose-your-own poke with more than 10,000 combinations and a new seasonal poke each month (Tabelog, shop-provided).
chef_bio.specialty: Custom poke bowls; garlic shrimp; mochiko chicken; açaí bowl.

anecdotes.text: "The garlic shrimp was so tender that you could eat the shells, and the garlic flavor was strong, making it a great accompaniment to rice." — March 2026, Original Poke Bowl, Garlic Shrimp Plate, Mochiko Chicken and fries.
"The Poké Bowl with additional ingredients costs JPY 1350. It used to be under JPY 1000 not long ago." — April 2025.

osaka_wagashi_hiroido_shinmachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; many sweets are rice-based (daifuku, mochi, dango), but fu manju is made with wheat gluten, the baked sweets, pies and dorayaki are wheat-based, and the chestnut steamed yokan recipe is not stated. Ask about each sweet.
osaka_wagashi_hiroido_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Ask. Much of the range is bean paste, rice and agar, but some sweets use egg-yolk bean paste, condensed milk, cream cheese, honey or butter and cream; ask about each sweet.
osaka_wagashi_hiroido_shinmachi.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 9:00–18:00; closed Sunday, Monday and holidays, plus some irregular days; hours can shift on event days (Tabelog; shop site). Mainly takeout with 2 seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Reservations taken by phone even for a single sweet; fresh sweets (namagashi) are sold by reservation (Tabelog; shop catalog). Payment: Tabelog lists QR only, no cards; the shop site lists cash, PayPay, Osaka premium vouchers and VISA, Mastercard, JCB, AMEX. Chestnut steamed yokan (栗むし羊羹) is seasonal: in 2026 from 21 September to late December, handed over from about 11:00, reservation only, no same-day sales, chilled shipping available (shop site). Founded in Meiji 10 (1877) (shop site).
osaka_wagashi_hiroido_shinmachi.notes: [Wagashi · Shinmachi, a 150-year-old sweets shop run by a couple] A small Japanese-sweets shop founded in 1877 in Shinmachi, a former geisha district; the shop's sign survived the wartime fires and the shop was revived after the war. Today a married couple makes and sells everything, which is why the famous autumn chestnut steamed yokan (hand-peeled chestnuts, Hokkaido bean paste, ¥3,000 for a half) is reservation-only and gone by late December. Year-round there is Yūgiri monaka with the shell kept crisp until you buy it and a bear-shaped honey cream cheese monaka; in summer Warawazu mochi (somewhere between water yokan and mochi), bouncy mizu manju, fu manju and a fruit kanten where the watermelon is still crunchy; in September Osaka-style moon-viewing dango. One diner calls the cream-and-butter dorayaki the best ever. In August 2026 a diner waited behind a couple of customers. Closed Sunday and Monday.

chef_bio.chef_name: 小澤康雄・小澤ゆう子
roles: Owners (a married couple), who make and sell the sweets
chef_bio.background: The shop was founded in Meiji 10 (1877) in Shinmachi, once a hanamachi; the signboard escaped the wartime fires and, "like a baton passed to the third generation", let 御菓子司 廣井堂 be revived after the war. It is now run by the married couple 小澤康雄 and 小澤ゆう子, and the couple make and sell everything (shop site, read October 2026: "小澤康雄・小澤ゆう子 夫婦にて"; the chestnut yokan page says the two make and sell everything, so mass production is hard).
chef_bio.philosophy: A small shop aiming for taste and service that please each customer; a writer once described it as "変わりゆく町の変わらない味" (the unchanging taste of a changing town) (shop site).
chef_bio.specialty: Chestnut steamed yokan; Yūgiri monaka; honey cream cheese monaka; Warawazu mochi.

anecdotes.text: "The firm texture of the monaka shell, which isn't soggy, pairs beautifully with the refined sweetness of the filling… The owner's service was exceptional." — August 2025, Yūgiri Monaka to take away.
"The watermelon is crunchy, and the other fruits don't feel mushy at all; you can really tell they were just peeled!" — September 2025, fruit kanten.

osaka_milia_burger_shinmachi.notes: [Burgers · Shinmachi, choose every layer] A calm, café-like burger shop in the stylish Shinmachi area that opened in 2016 billing itself as Japan's first custom-burger specialist. Pick a brown, white or whole-wheat bun (or lettuce instead), a beef patty, pork rib or chicken leg, one of ten house-made sauces and three vegetables, or order a set burger like the Tex-Mex with avocado and jalapeños or the ABC. Diners single out the patty: coarse-ground with steak-like chunks, cooked rare and juicy enough to soak the bun. The owner explained the menu to one first-time diner in May 2026. One diner found it pricey for the size. Sofas and a terrace; open until 9 pm Thursday to Saturday, and fine for just a drink.

chef_bio.background: Custom-burger shop that opened on 16 June 2016, billed by the shop as Japan's first custom burger specialty shop (Tabelog, shop-provided). Diners mention the owner explaining the menu (May and July 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Build your own burger: 1.2 million combinations per the shop site (Tabelog's shop text says 13.5 million), all sauces made in-house (shop site).
chef_bio.specialty: Custom burgers; chunky rare-cooked patties.

anecdotes.text: "Upon entering, the owner kindly explained the menu… the original Tex-Mex Burger for JPY 1,668… The meat sauce tied everything together beautifully, with a delightful kick from the jalapeños." — May 2026.
"Inside the coarsely ground meat, there are tender chunks, providing a texture close to steak… The meat is cooked rare." — July 2026, ABC Burger ¥1,668.

osaka_futsuni_fruits_minamisenba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the food is fruit sandwiches on bread and baked goods. Only the drinks (hand-drip coffee, tea, juices, cream soda) are free of bread.
osaka_futsuni_fruits_minamisenba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the fruit sandwiches are made with cream cheese or flavoured cream, and the strawberry milk and cream soda carry ice cream. The Japanese apple and mikan juices are the plain options.
osaka_futsuni_fruits_minamisenba.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–16:00; closing days not fixed (Tabelog, shop site). Seats can be reserved through Tabelog; items can then be reserved by Instagram message; no same-day reservations; at busy times seating is limited to one hour (Tabelog). Order and pay at the entrance, then sit (April–July 2026 reviews). Tabelog says cashless payment only (cards, IC cards, PayPay); an August 2026 review says cash or PayPay only — check. 14 seats; non-smoking (Tabelog). Opened 22 February 2024 (Tabelog). Up the stairs at the side of the building; the entrance is shared with Pan to Espresso to and is easy to miss (June–July 2026 reviews).
osaka_futsuni_fruits_minamisenba.notes: [Kissa · Minamisenba, fruit sandwiches upstairs in a former bank] A fruit kissa on the second floor of the Sakaisuji Club, a building that went up as a bank in 1931 (April 2026 review); Pan to Espresso to bakes on the ground floor, and the same company runs both. The entrance and staircase are grand, the room is retro and calm, with many clocks, tables stamped with fruit patterns and a wall of manga to read. The draw is the thick-cut fruit sandwich: figs, orange and kiwi with cream cheese, white peach with Earl Grey cream, American cherries with chocolate cream — the fruit changes with the season. A strawberry milk topped with ice cream and fresh strawberries is the other favourite. Diners may also bring up bread bought downstairs and re-toast it here, so seats fill fast: reserve, or come early. One July 2026 diner found the peach disappointing and smelled frying from the kitchen below.

chef_bio.background: Run directly by 株式会社パンとエスプレッソと (Pan to Espresso to Co.), listed under its "other shops" on the company site; the company's Pan to Espresso to bakery café occupies the 1F of the same building (shop site). Opened 22 February 2024 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fruit sandwiches made with seasonal fruit (June 2026 review; official menu "from ¥1,400").
chef_bio.specialty: Fruit sandwiches; strawberry milk.

anecdotes.text: "The building, constructed in 1931 as a bank, exudes a sense of grandeur. The first floor houses 'Pan to Espresso to,' while this café is on the second floor." — April 2026, strawberry milk ¥700.

"Some customers order from 'Futsuni Fruits,' while others bring in bread purchased from the first floor's 'Bread and Espresso' to enjoy in the 'Futsuni Fruits' dining area, making the seating fill up quite quickly." — June 2026, weekday 11:30 reservation.

osaka_fukushima_coffee_cafe_de_rope_inar.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the food is toast, sandwiches and hot dogs. Coffee, juice, boiled eggs and bananas are the bread-free choices.
osaka_fukushima_coffee_cafe_de_rope_inar.vegan_detail: Not vegan: egg and cheese toasts, egg sandwiches and hot dogs; café au lait and lattes are made with milk. Black coffee, mixed juice (ask) and bananas are the options.
osaka_fukushima_coffee_cafe_de_rope_inar.hours_raw: Tue–Sat and public holidays 8:00–16:00; closed Sunday and Monday, and over the summer holidays and long weekends such as Golden Week; hours may change, so check (Tabelog). Coffee is paid for at the register and the staff make it (May 2025 review). Cards, IC cards, Rakuten Edy, nanaco, WAON, iD, QUICPay; QR payments accepted (Tabelog). 20 seats including counter seats with power outlets and a terrace; non-smoking, including the terrace and e-cigarettes; wheelchair accessible; free Wi-Fi (Tabelog; February 2026 review). Children welcome, but noisy children are not, as some guests read (Tabelog). Paid parking nearby. Opened 13 October 1988 (Tabelog).
osaka_fukushima_coffee_cafe_de_rope_inar.notes: [Coffee stand · Inari near JR Namba, a roaster dealer's own café since 1988] The street smells of roasting coffee before you reach the door. This is the café of Fukushima Coffee, a company that sells, installs and repairs coffee roasters (it is the Japan agent for DIEDRICH), and gleaming machines stand on display behind the big windows; one diner was told a single FUJI ROYAL roaster costs as much as a domestic car. The coffee is roasted in-house and cheap for Namba: ¥250 to take away, ¥300 to sit, and the beans are for sale. Food is light and quick: cheese toast, a hefty tamagoyaki sandwich, a small soft hot dog, ¥50 boiled eggs and half-bananas. There is a roomy seating area at the back, counter seats with outlets for laptops, and a terrace. One diner first came before getting married and still stops by with mom after neighbourhood errands (2024–2025 reviews).

chef_bio.background: The café department, at the head office, of 株式会社福島珈琲 (Fukushima Coffee Co.), whose representative is 福島建三 (company site). The company sells new and used coffee roasters, is the Japan agent for DIEDRICH, and roasts and sells beans; the café shows roasters from several makers and does test roasts (company site). Opened 13 October 1988 (Tabelog). Once delivered lunches and served rice dishes, salads and cold noodles; by February 2024 the food was toasts and sandwiches, and the owner makes them right after the order (February 2024 review); by May 2024 the business focus had shifted to selling and maintaining roasters (May 2024 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Full support for customers' coffee businesses, from roasters to green-bean quality (company site).
chef_bio.specialty: Coffee roasted in-house; cheap takeaway coffee; toasts and sandwiches.

osaka_stand_soba_sankaku_minamisenba.notes: [Soba · Minamisenba, juwari soba by day and a late soba bar by night] A soba shop on Yokobori-suji that looks more like a stylish bar (one diner calls the interior rock and roll), with a whisky bottle on the counter even at lunch. The soba is juwari, 100% buckwheat, on the thick and firm side and strongly aromatic, so firm that one diner wondered whether it was really juwari. At lunch the soba comes with a bowl of mixed rice and a small side: horumon soba with a clear, delicate broth, a ginger-thickened chicken-and-egg soba for cold days, bukkake soba with ume and shirasu, and a large mori soba whose size made one diner laugh. Try a bite with the seaweed, curry or matcha salt before the rich katsuobushi dipping sauce, and finish with the thick soba-yu. From 19:00 it turns soba izakaya, with oden, fried loach, crab miso, mozuku tempura and sake from around Japan, open until 3 am (5 am on Friday and Saturday). An August 2026 diner recalls branches in Awaza, Fukushima and Ura-Namba that have since gone, and says the owner is now different.

An August 2026 diner remembers branches in Awaza, Fukushima and Ura-Namba that no longer exist, and says the owner is now different. Two people run lunch on a busy weekday (November 2025 review); a manager is on the floor (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: 100% buckwheat soba paired with seasonal sake; daily specials so there is something new to discover (Tabelog, shop-provided).

osaka_mochisho_shizuku_shinmachi.gf_detail: Some options, by the shop's own ingredient lists: the Shinmachi classics (black-bean mochi, kusa mochi, raspberry daifuku, kuro mochi, monaka, chestnut daifuku, shigure, kurumi mochi) list glutinous rice, rice flour, mochi flour, potato starch, beans, sugar, salt and fruit, and no wheat. The shop makes no gluten-free claim and says nothing about cross-contact, and the Kanro tea-room course includes savoury mochi dishes that are not listed, so ask at the counter.
osaka_mochisho_shizuku_shinmachi.vegan_detail: Some options, by the shop's own ingredient lists: black-bean mochi, kusa mochi, raspberry daifuku, kuro mochi, monaka, chestnut daifuku, shigure, kurumi mochi, chestnut chakin and ginkgo daifuku list only plant ingredients. Not vegan: the Mont Blanc (fresh cream, October 2026 review), fruit daifuku with cream, the Kishiwada-shop sweets made with honey, and the Kanro course (a mochi soup with crab, October 2026 review).
osaka_mochisho_shizuku_shinmachi.hours_raw: Daily: shop 10:30–18:00; open year-round, closures announced on the website (mochi-shizuku.jp; Tabelog). Tea room "Kanro" (甘露), opened in the renovated shop in 2026: by reservation, two seatings a day at 13:00 and 15:00, a pairing course of sweets, mochi dishes and tea ¥6,600 per person including tax, sake or a non-alcoholic drink extra; book by phone or through the online shop (prepaid online), no cancellations, walk-ins if a seat is free; junior-high age and up only; mention allergies when booking (shop notice, 15 October 2026). The old casual eat-in café is gone (October 2026 reviews); about six chairs outside (October 2026 review). Cards (VISA, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 8 counter seats listed; non-smoking; wheelchair access (Tabelog). Renamed from 日月餅 on 1 July 2011 (Tabelog). Tabelog Sweets WEST 100 2018–2020 and 2022; Wagashi WEST 100 2023 and 2026.
osaka_mochisho_shizuku_shinmachi.notes: [Wagashi · Shinmachi, mochi from pesticide-free ingredients in a gallery-like shop] A wagashi maker that pounds its mochi daily in a sunken machine made more than 30 years ago and in use since the previous generation, and uses naturally farmed, pesticide-free glutinous rice, azuki, rice flour and sugar from contract growers across western Japan, testing each new harvest for radiation. The Shinmachi shop, renovated in 2026, looks like a concrete art gallery, with sweets laid out like jewels. The signature is the black-bean mochi, studded with big Tanba beans salt-boiled every morning around smooth bean paste; around it run a beet-red raspberry daifuku with white bean paste and rum, chestnut chakin and a pure-chestnut Mont Blanc in autumn, and fruit daifuku through the year. Behind a low crawl-through door the shop opened Kanro, a dim, quiet tea room serving a reserved four-course pairing of sweets and mochi dishes, a drink matched to each; an October 2026 guest had a crystal-like jelly with azuki tea, a hozuki daifuku, a mochi soup topped with crab and a chestnut kinton, then a Panama coffee cloth-dripped by the owner. Prices run high; popular items sell out, so go early. The owner, 石田, invites questions about the growers.

chef_bio.background: Wagashi maker with shops in Shinmachi (renamed from 日月餅 to Mochisho Shizuku on 1 July 2011, Tabelog), Kishiwada (where the workshop is) and Ashiya (『上』); the mochi machine has been used since the previous generation (shop website). The Shinmachi tea room ran for eighteen years before the January 2026 renovation (shop notice, 20 January 2026). The tea room Kanro opened in the renovated shop (shop notices, October 2026).
chef_bio.philosophy: Sweets as "the chief of a hundred medicines": naturally farmed, pesticide-free ingredients from contract growers, harvests tested for radiation each year; best mochi from "human plus machine" (shop website). Kanro is a "mountain retreat in the city", a designed quiet (shop notice, 15 October 2026).
chef_bio.specialty: Black-bean mochi with Tanba black beans; raspberry daifuku; seasonal chestnut sweets.

anecdotes.text: "The surface of the mochi is dotted with black beans, which are the finest quality from Tanba, Hyogo Prefecture, and are boiled in salt every morning at the shop." — October 2026, takeout.

Lunch reservations only for the 11:00 opening; late arrivals may lose the seat to people waiting (Tabelog; an August 2026 diner arrived 2–3 minutes late and waited 30 minutes outside). Evening table charge ¥500, waived with a drink (Tabelog; June 2026 review). Order by QR code on your phone (2026 reviews). osaka_spice_stand_tongari_shinmachi.notes: [Curry · Shinmachi, a seven-seat spice-curry counter that turns dining bar at night] A small brick-walled counter with a natural-wood bar near the Orix Theater, run by one person, that opened in January 2025. Lunch is spice curry on a dashi base, usually two to a plate: the Tongari beef keema with its rich, spicy broth beside a yogurt-tart sour chicken, or rotating partners such as coconut pork belly, and lately game, with venison keema and a mild sour-butter duck. The plate comes heaped with fresh vegetables, achar, nuts and, unusually for spice curry, fukujinzuke and rakkyo. Rice sizes are named after mountains, from Osaka's tiny Tenpozan up to Everest. Order on your phone by QR code; a LINE sign-up gets a free pickled-egg topping. At night it becomes a dining bar with spiced snacks and fried Tajima chicken; a drink waives the ¥500 table charge. Lunch bookings are for 11:00 only, and the seat goes to the queue if you're late.

osaka_bistro_sifflet_shinmachi.notes: [French · Shinmachi, a one-person bistro of big plates and natural wine] A casual French bistro beside the Orix Theater, open since 2018, that cooks hearty dishes from organic vegetables grown by partner farms and pours natural wine chosen by the sommelier and chef. One person runs both the room and the kitchen, so plan on a long, relaxed meal; diners call the service warm and the explanations careful. Portions are generous: a thick Mita pork pâté en croûte, Mita pork with white beans in Madeira sauce, skirt steak with fries, crisp-skinned yellowtail, with house breads one diner asked to have refilled. Dinner is a ¥7,700 tasting menu, a ¥5,500 prix fixe or à la carte; lunch courses run ¥2,100 to ¥4,400 and fill by noon on Saturdays, so book. Leave the strong perfume at home.

osaka_vege_eats_hakurocho.notes: [Café · Hakurocho, a weekday fill-your-cup salad bar] A stylish, clean weekday salad shop between Sakaisuji-Hommachi and Nagahoribashi that grows its own lettuce hydroponically indoors and buys the rest of its vegetables straight from farmers. Crowded from noon with office workers; Utsubo Park is a walk away for a picnic.

osaka_hong_kong_ebisuhigashi.notes: [Local Chinese · Shinsekai, a one-person Showa counter under Tsutenkaku] A narrow ten-seat counter behind red lanterns and a red noren, a few steps from Tsutenkaku, open only in the evening and run by a single cook who works the kitchen at the back. The owner told one diner the shop has been here about 60 years, passed down from the previous generation, and that the name is not about Hong Kong at all: it is short for 'Kagawa's port', after Kagawa roots. Nearly everyone orders the Tonkara, a whole thick cut of pork (loin or chuck eye roll, both shown to you before you choose) fried crisp and juicy, so big that one diner took the rest home; it comes with mustard-vinegar soy sauce, and half portions are refused because a smaller piece would not taste right. Around it: oily, salty stir-fries made for bottled beer, moist fried rice, an off-menu omurice, a light shio ramen for ¥500. The seats fill within minutes of the 17:00 opening, orders wait their turn because one person cooks everything, and one diner had doubts about cleanliness; another calls it the epitome of local Chinese food.

The ice is fluffy but holds its shape, comes generous and photogenic, and is topped with your choice of almond or yogurt espuma — the almond one diner found 'shockingly good'; flavors run from strawberry milk and white chocolate to jasmine tea and black sugar douhua. Kakigori starts at noon and can take a while in summer. The tapioca drinks are huge and cheap for the area, with half-price takeout during time sales. At lunch the creamy soy-milk tantanmen is gentle rather than fiery; add rice if you must, though two diners thought it not worth the ¥220.

osaka_kamokin_ebisu_honten.notes: [Udon · Shinsekai, the 2005 head shop of a duck dipping-noodle brand] A ten-seat counter a few minutes from Tsutenkaku that serves one thing: a hot dipping sauce crowded with thin slices of duck, tiny dried fish, quail egg, lemon and green onion, and your choice of udon, soba or Chinese noodles in one, two or three servings (regulars go for three, one diner says). The duck fat makes it rich and the lemon keeps it bright. When the noodles are gone, pour the ginger hot water from the tokkuri into what is left and drink it down. The founding story on the official site: at 48, with ¥2 million in hand, the founder recalled a tsuke kamo udon shop loved in leaner days and long gone, spent six months on a men-tsuyu to beat it, and opened on a main street; five of the six first-day customers came back the next day. This counter, opened in December 2005, became the head shop. One long-time diner noticed new staff, a slightly changed name and higher prices in 2026, but the same taste. Lunch only, cash only, and it can sell out early.

The aim is Chinese food that isn't heavy: the stocks, chili oil and sauces are all blended in-house. Its calling card is the white mapo tofu, milder than the red one (also on the menu) and best ordered, one diner insists, with the bright green spinach fried rice; diners add the yuba-wrapped shumai, the steamed chicken with chili oil, and whatever is on the blackboard — horse-meat carpaccio, cold summer stir-fries with green peppers, jellyfish, crab potato salad. One diner sees a French touch in the plating, the highballs come with bear- or rose-shaped ice, and diners describe a kind manager to chat with at the counter.

osaka_shinmachi_wakei.gf_detail: Ask. The shop asks to be told about food allergies when booking and offers to adjust dishes, but makes no gluten-free claim; tempura comes with nearly every set and course, and the shabu-shabu uses a house dipping sauce.
osaka_shinmachi_wakei.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the cooking is built on a dashi of Rishiri kelp and honkarebushi bonito (Tabelog, shop-provided), and the sets and courses centre on fish, shrimp, pork and beef.
osaka_shinmachi_wakei.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–14:00 (last order 13:30) and 18:00–24:00; lunch closes if there are no reservations, dinner by reservation only and same-day bookings may not be possible because of market closures; closing days not fixed (late May listed); the shop will try to take bookings outside these hours (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 15 seats: a counter (about five to seven seats per 2023–2024 reviews) and one sunken-kotatsu private room for 4–8, which may refuse children when booked for business; whole-shop booking up to 20; smoking only in the private room at night (Tabelog). osaka_shinmachi_wakei.notes: [Kaiseki · Shinmachi, a hideaway for seasonal Japanese cooking at honest prices] A small Japanese restaurant tucked into the ground floor of an apartment block near Nishi-Ohashi, opened in 2017 by a chef who trained at a long-established Osaka restaurant and was head chef at the Michelin-starred Sōsaku Ryori Kawahara in Ehime, the chef's home prefecture. Everything rests on a delicate dashi of Rishiri kelp and honkarebushi. Lunch is the draw: the Wakei set lays out about a dozen bite-sized seasonal dishes (sesame tofu, duck, fried horse mackerel, vegetable jellies) with seasonal rice, and the fuller version adds two sashimi and tempura, the thick-cut eggplant and the sweet Awaji onion singled out by diners. Kaiseki lunches and dinner omakase run up to fugu, wagyu shabu-shabu and matsutake in season. There is a counter and one sunken-kotatsu private room, popular for family celebrations; a 90-year-old guest who could not eat raw food was cooked for and finished everything (April 2026). Everything is by reservation; lunch closes when nobody has booked.

osaka_nunome_no_sato_shinmachi.notes: [Shokudo · Shinmachi, vegetable-packed set meals from a Nara village] A clean little set-meal shop with a counter and three tables that sources its vegetables from Yamazoe Village in Nara and its fish straight from Wakayama, and sells some of that produce at the door. Every set comes with a pile of vegetables: a salad with a vegetable dressing, two small sides (wasabi-leaf ohitashi, stir-fried shirataki, wakame) and rice mixed with hijiki, grains or whatever is in season. Favourites are the ginger pork, the pork steak under green-onion sauce, the simmered fish, and the juhosai, an oyster-sauce stir-fry so full of vegetables one diner could not count them. The master cooks everything alone, so a crowd can mean a wait, and it fills with office workers by 12:10; diners call the master and staff kind. Cash only.

osaka_hanahiraku_agu_tonkatsu_shinmachi.notes: [Tonkatsu · Shinmachi, a seven-seat counter for Okinawan Agu pork] The shop of the pork-specialist cook known on social media as Gotton, who moved it from Fuse to Shinmachi in November 2025. It serves only Okinawan Agu pork, some 14 or 15 kinds from Okinawa, Ishigaki and the nearby islands, aged in-house for two weeks or more, down to rare purebred lines such as Manten Aguu Kuro Maru. The cutlets are "white": fried slowly below 130°C in a light crumb, so the coating stays pale and the pink meat juicy, with the sweet, clean fat diners keep mentioning. Courses pair tasting cuts with Agu shabu-shabu, three sauces including a sansho ponzu, a dashi omelette, rice cooked per person, and black curry simmered for 30 hours from the bones; finish with the white-miso pudding. From November 2026 there is no lunch: one 18:30 seating for seven, courses only, booked a month ahead.

osaka_betsubara_shinmachi.notes: [Sweets · Shinmachi, reservation-only kakigori built on fresh fruit] A small, bright shaved-ice shop north of Nishi-Ohashi Station, open since 2013, where the menu turns with the fruit season and the bookings go fast. In summer the peach is the prize: the fruit is blended to order into a 100% peach syrup sweeter than the peaches on top, and it often sells out by evening. Around it come watermelon, melon with mascarpone, chocolate-mint melon and cherries; autumn brings pear or fig with the shop's signature "cheese tea" of Earl Grey syrup and cheese sauce; winter and spring bring strawberries, pistachio and mochi-paste versions. A June 2026 diner rated the pistachio the best pistachio kakigori ever eaten. The room is quiet enough that the loudest sound is the ice being shaved, and warm tea comes in a small paper cup. Book the day before through the link on the shop's Instagram.

osaka_fukumitsuya_tokuimachi.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; the menu runs to gyoza, spring rolls, kara-age, sweet-and-sour pork, dan dan noodles and crispy yakisoba, and sauces are not described.
osaka_fukumitsuya_tokuimachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: pork, chicken, shrimp, squid and scallop dishes; nothing described as vegan.
osaka_fukumitsuya_tokuimachi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:30–23:00 (last order 22:30); closed Sunday and public holidays, and over Golden Week, Obon and New Year (Tabelog). Reservations accepted; private hire for 8 or more with a minimum order of ¥4,000 a head (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX) (Tabelog). The English listing's automatic translation mentions a 10% service charge, but the original Japanese text it shows says なし (none). 13 seats: 7 at the counter, 6 at tables; smoking allowed (Tabelog; a November 2025 review confirms smoking inside). One person cooks and serves, so dishes can take a while at busy times (Tabelog; 2025 reviews).
osaka_fukumitsuya_tokuimachi.notes: [Chinese · Tanimachi 4-chome, a one-person bistro counter] A dark, slightly forbidding front opens onto a black, bar-like room with a hand-painted dragon on the wall, seven counter seats and a couple of tables. One chef, with 30 years in Chinese kitchens by the shop's own account, cooks and serves everything, so dishes come at their own pace; diners say the wait pays. Solo drinkers start with the ¥1,100 evening set (a drink plus five small plates) or the ¥1,600 tasting set that ends in a mini dan dan noodles, numbing and properly spicy. The sweet-and-sour pork sits on a bed of crisp fried spring-roll skins, the mapo tofu arrives bubbling in a cast-iron pot with a rich, deep flavour rather than Sichuan heat, and a regular never skips the shrimp, scallop and cheese egg stir-fry. Smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: A Chinese chef with 30 years of experience (Tabelog, shop-provided text). Diners describe a one-person operation in which the owner cooks and serves (March, June and August 2025 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Authentic Chinese cooking that brings out the natural flavour of the ingredients, at reasonable prices, with counter seats for solo diners (Tabelog, shop-provided text).
chef_bio.specialty: Mapo tofu; sweet-and-sour pork on fried spring-roll skins; set menus.

anecdotes.text: "It seems the owner manages everything alone, so there was a bit of a wait from ordering to serving, but it was a perfect amount of time to enjoy my mild buzz." — March 2025, evening drink set ¥1,100.
"I love Mapo Tofu, and I've had it at many Chinese restaurants, but this might be my favorite! It's not the typical Sichuan style; it has a rich and deep flavor." — February 2026.

osaka_china_dining_alpha_tennoji.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: pork, chicken, beef and shrimp dishes; nothing described as vegan.

Dinner by reservation only; reservations taken for dinner only; tell the shop about allergies or dislikes when booking (Tabelog). osaka_china_dining_alpha_tennoji.notes: [Chinese · Tennoji, a couple-run hideaway across from Isshinji Temple] An easy-to-miss restaurant in the ground floor of an apartment block facing Isshinji Temple. Diners say the owner-chef spent 15 years as head chef of a well-known restaurant and won the grand prize at a Chinese cooking competition, and a newspaper article on the wall tells of years leading a renowned Sichuan kitchen; celebrity autographs hang here and there. The cooking is refined rather than greasy. Lunch is good value: the signature dan dan noodles (choose the heat), sweet-and-sour pork set with soup and lychee, or a light, spicy curry fried rice with the house kara-age. Dinner is by reservation: a ¥5,500 course might bring stir-fried beef with miso tucked into steamed buns and sizzling crispy rice. Regulars mention the warmth of the master and the master's wife, and an owner who sees guests out the door.

chef_bio.background: Served 15 years as head chef at a famous restaurant and won the grand prize in a Chinese cooking competition (September 2025 and September 2026 reviews, the latter citing the shop's Tabelog page). A newspaper article displayed in the restaurant says the master was head chef at a renowned Sichuan restaurant for many years (September 2024 review). Runs the shop with the master's wife (July 2025 and September 2024 reviews). Tabelog notes a move from Ōsu, Nagoya.
chef_bio.specialty: Dan dan noodles; sweet-and-sour pork; dinner courses.

osaka_kuune_awajicho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a chicken restaurant; the noodles and mapo tofu are topped with minced chicken.
osaka_kuune_awajicho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–12:45 (last entry for lunch) and 17:30–21:30; Sat 17:30–21:30; closed Sunday, public holidays and every other Saturday — check the monthly calendar (Tabelog). Lunch serves only dan dan noodles and chicken mapo tofu; order and pay at once (2023–2025 reviews); mostly business people at lunch (2022 review). Yakitori and tsukune at night. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB) and PayPay; no e-money (Tabelog). 15 seats: 7 at the counter, two tables of 4; non-smoking (Tabelog). Bentos under the name Kuune Bento (Instagram kuune_obento, per Tabelog).
osaka_kuune_awajicho.notes: [Yakitori · Awajicho, a couple's tsukune bar that sells dan dan noodles at lunch] A dim, homey room on the ground floor of Rejoice Awajicho, run by a couple: the chef in the kitchen, the partner out front. At night it is a charcoal yakitori and tsukune bar — order skewers singly to try more, with salt, shiso-kombu or miso-mayo tsukune, shrimp and cheese versions, and egg rice to finish. At lunch the counter fills with office workers for just two things: chicken mapo tofu, eaten like curry, and soupless dan dan noodles, the house signature. Flat, chewy noodles come in a curry plate under spiced minced chicken, black and white sesame and tahini, bok choy, sushi-style pickled ginger and crunchy kaki-pi; pick the simple black-sesame bowl or the numbing Sichuan one, add rice to mop up the sauce, and borrow the apron provided. One noodle critic found the flavour lacking; most come back.

chef_bio.background: Run by two people, the head chef in the kitchen and a hostess serving customers (December 2022 review); described as a couple (December 2023 and February 2024 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Charcoal-grilled chicken and tsukune; soupless dan dan noodles; chicken mapo tofu.

osaka_karashogun_enokojima.vegan_detail: Not vegan in practice: the menu runs to fried chicken, shrimp and clams, and no plant-based tantanmen or mapo is mentioned.
osaka_karashogun_enokojima.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:00 and 18:00–23:00; Sat and public holidays 18:00–23:00 (no lunch); closed Sunday (Tabelog). Obon: dinner only on 11–16 August (Tabelog). One May 2025 diner found it closed on weekends. Reservations accepted; no cards, other payment not listed (Tabelog). 20 seats; no smoking at lunch, smoking allowed in the evening bar hours (Tabelog). Spice is chosen when ordering, in five levels per a February 2025 review; lunch queues of office workers (2025 reviews). Opened 20 November 2016 (Tabelog). osaka_karashogun_enokojima.notes: [Ramen · Awaza, a Sichuan tantanmen counter under a painted Shoki] A small Chinese bar in an office building a minute from Awaza Station, behind a bold sign, where the owner is said to have painted the imposing wall mural of Shoki, and the chef speaks Chinese. Tantanmen is the point: around ten kinds, five spice levels, and three noodles to choose from (thin, medium-thick, or the rarer flat ones). The original Sichuan bowl brings numbing peppercorn and star anise, the white-sesame one is tangier and gentle, and 'regular' heat already makes some diners sweat — though others found medium mild. At lunch, office workers queue for sets pairing tantanmen with the even hotter mapo rice; dishes come as they are ready, finished with a few canned mandarin segments. A regular since opening felt the flavours drifted in September 2026, and another diner got overcooked noodles, but the owner's generosity (free rice, almond tofu, a rounded-down bill) wins people over.

chef_bio.background: Opened 20 November 2016 (Tabelog). osaka_coffee_shop_erika_namba_walk.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the food is toast, sandwiches, hot dogs, pasta and pancakes. Coffee and the boiled egg that comes with the morning sets are the wheat-free items.
osaka_coffee_shop_erika_namba_walk.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the morning sets come with a boiled egg, the sandwiches hold egg and ham, the hot dogs a sausage, and the toast is topped with cheese; lattes and cappuccinos use milk. Black coffee is the option.

Morning menu 7:00–11:00 (April 2025 and January 2026 reviews); a January 2026 diner found the light meals are a separate menu that starts later (the diner guessed 11:00). Order and pay first at the counter (June 2025, January–February 2026 reviews). Smoking: reviews from October 2024 to January 2026 say every seat allows smoking (an October 2024 review: it moved from a designated smoking area to full smoking; a January 2025 review: so under-18s may not enter), and the Namba Walk page lists 喫煙可能; Tabelog still says "designated smoking area" with 8 non-smoking seats added — expect smoke. osaka_coffee_shop_erika_namba_walk.notes: [Kissa · Namba Walk, a smokers' coffee stand at the ticket gate] A Showa-style coffee shop in the Namba Walk underground mall, right by the Midosuji Line Namba Station ticket gate and the escalator up to Kintetsu Osaka-Namba. The kitchen sits inside a horseshoe counter, with a few tables in the middle; you order and pay first, and the food comes almost at once. It opens at 7:00, and the morning sets are the draw: a mini egg-and-ham sandwich, a hot dog with curry-flavoured cabbage, or cheese toast, each about ¥500 with a drink; the sandwich and hot dog sets add a boiled egg. One January 2026 diner called the price low enough to surprise even Nagoya. Later in the day there are sandwich sets, a pasta set and pancakes. This is one of the few cafés left where every seat allows smoking, and it is popular with salarymen; non-smokers in the 2025–2026 reviews found the smoke hard going. The coffee draws mixed notes, from aromatic to merely average, and one diner found it lukewarm.

chef_bio.background: A long-established coffee shop near the station (January 2025 review); Tabelog reviews go back to March 2017. The Namba Walk shop page lists it in the 1-bangai section as a coffee stand serving freshly ground coffee with toast and hot dogs.
chef_bio.philosophy: Freshly ground coffee to stop in for between work and shopping, with toast and hot dogs; a horseshoe counter with a grown-up feel (Namba Walk shop page).
chef_bio.specialty: Cheap morning sets; coffee where smoking is allowed.

osaka_chuka_tonton_edobori.notes: [Ramen · Edobori, a TV-famous machi-chuka and its curry champon] A homely local Chinese restaurant five minutes from Higobashi Station, with a short counter and four tables, featured on TV by Kendo Kobayashi as a local Chinese spot; several March–April 2026 diners came after seeing it on TV. Almost everyone orders a noodle soup, and above all the curry champon: chicken broth and soy sauce with a blended spicy curry powder, on thin straight noodles rather than the usual thick champon noodles, loaded with bean sprouts, cabbage and garlic chives. One diner found it addictive, another rather mild and reached for the chili oil. It comes as a ¥950 set with a small, moist fried rice (March 2026), good dipped in the curry soup. One regular always orders the light, comforting Yumen; another liked the tanmen packed with bean sprouts and cabbage. In the evening there is gyoza, house-made, full of vegetables and peppery, which one diner says made the visit worthwhile. One diner saw the owner apparently cooking everything alone in the lunch rush. Cash only, and smoking is allowed at the tables.

chef_bio.background: Local Chinese restaurant; the owner cooks everything alone at lunch (June 2026 review). Featured on TV by Kendo Kobayashi as a local Chinese restaurant (August 2026 review); a March 2026 diner came the day after a TV feature (March 2026 review).

osaka_oukan_abenobashi.notes: [Stand-up soba · Tennoji, a stair-landing noodle stop from 6 am] Hard to spot the first time: a noren on the landing of the stairs between the underground central gate of Kintetsu Osaka-Abenobashi Station and JR Tennoji, with standing room in front and a few chairs at the back. It opens at 6 am for commuters and travellers, and the prices are the draw: kake soba ¥320, tempura udon with shrimp and kakiage ¥440, and a one-coin set of soba, rice and a croquette for ¥500. The soy sauce goes into the bowl before the broth, the way a ramen shop does it, and diners praise the light Kansai dashi more than the noodles, which are soft in the stand-soba way; a few wanted more bonito, or a hotter bowl. Try the big kakiage, the kasu udon with fried pork fat, or the curry udon with braised beef. There is also an "Ekimae soba" with yellow Chinese noodles in the dashi. Cash at the ticket machine.

chef_bio.background: An old stand-up noodle shop on the Kintetsu Osaka-Abenobashi Station stairs; diners call it an old shop with character and a Showa-era feel (2024–2026 reviews). A September 2024 diner found it run by an older man and a young woman; a December 2025 diner was served by a friendly woman at the counter while the owner fried the kakiage and boiled the noodles. Diners disagree on the tempura: a December 2025 diner says it is commercial-grade, a January 2026 diner that all of it is made in-house by the chef.

Reviews differ on weekends: an April 2025 diner says Saturday is dinner only, and a September 2025 diner lists 16:30–21:30 on weekends and holidays, so check before a weekend lunch. Ramen at lunch; at night Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki, teppan dishes, side dishes and drinks, with the ramen still on offer (2025–2026 reviews). Reservations accepted (Tabelog). osaka_gu_teradacho.notes: [Ramen · Teradacho, shoyu ramen at lunch and Hiroshima okonomiyaki at night] A 20-seat neighbourhood place by the Teradacho crossing that changes with the clock: ramen at lunch, and at night Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki, a blackboard of side dishes and drinks, with the ramen still there to finish. Ramen fans come for a shoyu bowl compared to the Akira style: a sharp soy sauce over a pork-bone broth with an old-fashioned simmered-pork aroma, plenty of green onion and generous chashu. Shoyu and miso come "hearty", meaning about 200 g of thick, curly, chewy noodles instead of the medium-thin 130 g; shio is also on the menu. At lunch the kimchi is free, and rice is ¥200. The okonomiyaki is layered with crisp fried noodles and lots of cabbage, cut into pieces for easy eating. A friendly couple runs it, and diners talk about the regulars, and one found the owner remembered a customer from a single earlier ramen visit. Closed Tuesday; reviews disagree on weekend lunch.

The owner brought the side-dish menu over and remembered a diner who had come once before for ramen (May 2025 review). Diners mention many regulars (October 2025; April 2026).

osaka_piccolo_curry_namba_walk.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information for the curry sauce (the maker's retort version, sold as the shop's taste, lists spices, fruit, vegetables, beef, chutney and cream but no full ingredient list); the katsu curry and karaage are breaded or fried, so skip those.
osaka_piccolo_curry_namba_walk.vegan_detail: Not vegan: the signature Piccolo curry is a beef curry finished with cream (the maker's own description), the hayashi sauce is a brown sauce with loin meat finished with cream and yoghurt (also the maker's description), and the omurice is egg over chicken rice.
osaka_piccolo_curry_namba_walk.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–22:00, last order 21:30 (Piccolo shop list, read 2026-10-30); Tabelog gives 10:30–22:00, closed on irregular days and New Year's Day. Omurice is served 11:00–15:00 (July 2026 review). 8 counter seats, with the Namba Walk passage right behind them (Tabelog; August and October 2026 reviews). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). No reservations; non-smoking; takeout; the shop also sells the retort curries to take home (shop list: お持ち帰り・レトルトカレー販売店). Fukujinzuke pickles are free; rakkyo ¥110 (August 2026).
osaka_piccolo_curry_namba_walk.notes: [Curry · Namba Walk, the underground branch of an Umeda institution] A counter-only curry stand on the west side of the Namba Walk underground mall, so small that the walkway runs right behind your stool. Piccolo began in the Umeda underground mall over 40 years ago, by the maker's account (a 2026 review says over 50), and magazines once called it the "King of Curry". The house curry is a beef curry slow-cooked from thirty-odd spices with fruit and vegetables, rounded off with chutney and cream: sweet and rich rather than hot. For more heat there is a spicy curry with a lighter colour, and the "W sauce" puts both on one plate. Food comes fast, often within minutes, which suits a lunch break; free fukujinzuke sits on the counter. Katsu curry was ¥1,100 in August 2026, and omurice with tomato, curry or hayashi sauce runs ¥800–1,050 at lunch. Opinions run from "incredibly delicious" to "classic, just average". Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Run by ミツヤ食品工業株式会社 (head office Shinsaibashisuji 2-3-16; factory in Higashi-Osaka), which also makes Piccolo retort curries. The company's shop list names five Piccolo shops: Namba Walk, Whity Umeda, Hankyu Kappa Yokocho, JR Osaka Station and Nishinomiya Hankyu. Per the company site, Piccolo opened in the Umeda underground mall "over 40 years ago" as a pioneering curry specialist and was introduced as the "King of Curry" in magazines such as L Magazine; 2026 reviews give "nearly half a century" and "over 50 years". A long-time diner called the Namba Walk branch "Piccolo Junior", with a menu slightly different from Umeda's.
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh, carefully chosen ingredients, a blend of thirty-odd spices, and beef cooked separately so the meat itself can be tasted (company site).
chef_bio.specialty: Piccolo beef curry; spicy curry; the two together as the W sauce.

osaka_sushi_tempura_akira_sennichimae.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: half the menu is tempura and fried dishes (wheat batter), the sushi is eaten with soy sauce, and there is a ramen to finish. Sashimi exists, but there is no gluten information.
osaka_sushi_tempura_akira_sennichimae.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a seafood izakaya; the dashimaki is egg soaked in chicken broth (March 2025), the ramen is a sea-bream broth, and the tempura comes with a homemade dipping sauce whose makeup no source gives.
osaka_sushi_tempura_akira_sennichimae.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–16:00 (last order food 15:00, drinks 15:30) and 17:00–23:30 (last order food 22:30, drinks 23:00); closed on irregular days (Tabelog; reviews dated March 2025 and July 2026 give 12:00–23:30 and "Closed: Irregular holidays"). Appetizer charge ¥350 per person (Tabelog; a June 2026 diner's appetizer was katsuo tataki at ¥350); one drink per person is the rule (September 2026 review). Reservations taken; book ahead, it was nearly full on a weekday (September 2026 review); the all-you-can-eat sushi course is limited to three groups a day, by phone only (Tabelog). Cards, QUICPay, PayPay and Alipay accepted. 20 seats, counter and tables; non-smoking, with a smoking spot outside. English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Opened 5 September 2022 (Tabelog).
osaka_sushi_tempura_akira_sennichimae.notes: [Izakaya · Sennichimae, red-vinegar sushi and tempura from noon] A bright, casual sushi-and-tempura tavern a few minutes from Namba, open from noon, with fish bought at the market each morning. The sushi rice is seasoned with red vinegar and you can order a single piece (from ¥150 on the October 2026 menu). Two dishes are on almost every table: the "seafood overflow sushi", chunks of fish piled on a roll and buried in ikura (in May 2024 served to the beat of a drum), and rare salmon tempura with ikura tartare. The tempura is light and thin-battered, there are creative plates like a seafood yukhoe you tip out of its bowl, and a sea-bream broth ramen to finish. A 60-minute all-you-can-eat sushi course is limited to three groups a day. It is lively, young and full of overseas visitors, and the owner was described as young and friendly in 2025–2026. One October 2026 diner's reservation was not on file, and found the hamachi less than fresh.

chef_bio.background: Opened 5 September 2022 (Tabelog). A January 2023 diner wrote that "the experienced chef, who has worked at renowned restaurants, skillfully manages this establishment"; a March 2025 diner, that "a friendly young man who fits perfectly with the welcoming atmosphere runs the place"; a July 2026 diner, that "the charming and friendly owner runs the place with a refreshing demeanor". Tabelog mentions sake chosen by the manager. Reviews call it the Namba Shinsaibashi branch, but no other branch was found.
chef_bio.philosophy: Fresh fish from the market, sushi on a house blend of red vinegar from ¥110 a piece, and freshly fried tempura at casual prices (Tabelog shop description).
chef_bio.specialty: Seafood overflow sushi with ikura; rare salmon tempura with ikura tartare; red-vinegar nigiri by the piece.

anecdotes.text: "An entertaining dish where heaps of ikura (salmon roe) are generously piled on while the din-din drum plays!" — May 2024, seafood overflow sushi ¥1,958.
"The shrimp mayo served raw is a dish you don't hear about often, but the heads were crispy fried while the shrimp meat was fresh and raw." — September 2026.

osaka_italian_sakurai_soemoncho.gf_detail: Ask. No gluten information; fresh pasta is the heart of the menu, with garlic toast, gratins and a herb-crumb fish, though several pastas can be had as risotto (squid ink, gorgonzola, porcini) and there are grilled meats and carpaccio. Ask when booking.
osaka_italian_sakurai_soemoncho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: prosciutto, foie gras, crab, fish, lamb, beef and cheese run through the menu.
osaka_italian_sakurai_soemoncho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–24:00; closed Sunday, and occasionally on other days, so book first (Tabelog). Reservation only; parties of five or more take a course (Tabelog). Seat charge ¥550 per person, private rooms another ¥550 per person; one drink each, or ¥770 (Tabelog). Same-day cancellations are charged (Tabelog). Smoking allowed, so under-20s are not admitted; non-smokers are pointed to the private rooms (Tabelog). 18 seats: 6 at the counter and 2 private rooms (Tabelog). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). BYO and sommelier listed (Tabelog). Opened 17 December 2015 (Tabelog); closed for a time during COVID-19 and reopened (December 2021 review).
osaka_italian_sakurai_soemoncho.notes: [Italian · Soemoncho, a chef-sommelier's hideaway above the neon] An Italian restaurant on the fifth floor of a mixed-use building on busy Soemoncho street; one diner warned that the walk in makes first-timers wonder whether a restaurant can really be up there. Inside it is calm, with jazz, a six-seat counter and private rooms. It opened in December 2015; Chef Sakurai holds a sommelier certification, per a regular's 2020 review, and a 2024 review says the chef trained in Italy. The wine list is the other half of the draw: twenty-odd by the glass and over 300 bottles, with pairings matched to your taste, and a regular called the grappa selection perhaps the best in Osaka. Start with the assorted appetizer plate, where the crab-miso brûlée is the dish people remember, then fresh pasta, ordered to share. Several diners from 2021 to 2025 call it the best Italian in Minami, or in Osaka; one April 2025 diner found most dishes average. Smoking is allowed, so no under-20s.

roles: Chef (Tabelog: "authentic Italian cuisine crafted by Chef Sakurai")
chef_bio.background: Per the Tabelog shop description, Chef Sakurai has honed the craft over many years and cooks authentic Italian food "perfected by on-site exploration". A February 2024 diner wrote that the restaurant "is run by a chef who trained in authentic Italy". A long-time regular (July 2020 visit) wrote that "the owner-chef has a sommelier certification for wine". Opened 17 December 2015 (Tabelog); a regular who has come since the opening marked its 7th anniversary in December 2022. In October 2024 a diner saw the chef cooking and serving alone at 6 pm on a weekday; 2025–2026 reviews also mention staff.
chef_bio.philosophy: To deliver the true flavours of Italy: fresh pasta and appetizer plates, à la carte or as a course, paired with wine (Tabelog shop description).
chef_bio.specialty: Assorted appetizer plate with crab-miso brûlée; fresh pasta; wine pairings by the glass.

anecdotes.text: "It seemed like the chef was working alone; there were a couple of other groups besides us, but I didn't see any assistance throughout our time there." — October 2024.
"Located on the 5th floor of a mixed-use building, Sakurai has stayed there while many other suspicious places have turned over frequently on the same floor." — December 2022.

osaka_izakaya_hisa_higashishinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the centre of the menu is breaded, deep-fried kushikatsu dipped in a shared sauce, along with fried chicken, fried Camembert and a baguette with the ajillo. No gluten-free dishes are marked.
osaka_izakaya_hisa_higashishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef, pork, chicken and seafood skewers, beef-tendon dote-yaki, dashi-rolled omelette, salmon dishes and prosciutto. Vegetable kushikatsu (eggplant, leek, potato, lotus root and more) are on the menu, but the batter and frying oil are not described, so ask.
osaka_izakaya_hisa_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–3:00 (last order 2:00); Sun 18:00–24:00 (last order 23:00); closing days not fixed, and it may close on Sundays or the last day of a holiday run (Tabelog). The shop's own site says 18:00–27:00 (food last order 26:00, drinks 26:30), closed Sunday unless booked ahead. Reservations accepted (Tabelog, which also takes bookings online). Cards: VISA and Master (Tabelog); the site also lists AMEX and Diners. Table charge (otoshi) ¥324 (Tabelog). 16 seats: 4 at the counter, 12 at tables; private hire for up to 20 (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog; an October 2023 diner: "Smoking is allowed at the table."). Courses with all-you-can-drink have a two-hour limit (an August 2026 review; the site: 120 minutes, last order at 90).
osaka_izakaya_hisa_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Izakaya · Higashi-Shinsaibashi, a late kushikatsu bar to melodic-hardcore records] A small kushikatsu bar on the ground floor of a tenant building just off Suo-cho street, in the thick of the Higashi-Shinsaibashi nightlife, open until 3:00. The shop calls itself a mix of Shinsekai-style kushikatsu and a Western bar: alongside the skewers, which you dip once in a shared stainless-steel tray of sweet, light sauce, there are ajillo, salmon carpaccio and caprese, dashi-rolled omelette and beef-tendon dote-yaki. Diners find the kushikatsu light and crisp, with a slightly coarser crumb than most Osaka shops, and one singled out the salmon (September 2025). Desserts are made by the owner, who has worked as a pastry chef. The music is loud melodic hardcore and punk, and records and bass guitars decorate the room. Several reviewers came for the ¥3,000 course with two hours of drinks and ten skewers each. Several 2023 reviews complained about service and cleanliness; later reviews mostly found the staff friendly. Smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Opened 1 April 2015 (Tabelog; the shop's blog on 30 March 2016: "四月一日に一周年になります"). The shop's site says the owner has worked as a pastry chef ("パティシエ経験ありのオーナーが作るデザート"); its Tabelog page (auto-translated) mentions "dishes by a French-trained owner" and calls it a family-run shop. A January 2026 diner found the manager serving every customer alone; a September 2024 diner had a good conversation with the owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: Osaka's famous kushikatsu fused with a bar: Shinsekai-style kushikatsu with Western dishes such as ajillo, prosciutto marinade and caprese, Japanese dishes too, and a daily dessert (shop site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kushikatsu with the shared sauce tray; homemade desserts.

anecdotes.text: "I was pleased to discover that the BGM was by Hi-STANDARD, a detail shared by my host, and I had a nice chat with the manager." — April 2022, two 10-skewer platters with dote-yaki and tako-wasa.
"In Osaka, many places serve finely crushed breadcrumbs, but here they use a slightly coarser texture that enhances the flavor of the ingredients." — November 2023.
"Despite being only JPY 3000, we received 10 skewers per person, and the variety of dishes was impressive." — June 2026, course with all-you-can-drink.
